This week the National Diet convened finally to address growing concerns within Japan, citing specifically the growing concerns of the apparent generation gap. At the current child birth rate analysts project a 25% drop in population by 2050, an end population estimated 95.5 Million people. With a staggering 20% of the population being 65 years or older in age with insufficient followup generation, experts fear for the coming generation. The topic had been extensively addressed in recent years with minimal observable changes in child birthrates. With the opening of the Diet this week talks were spurred by leading members of the Liberal Democratic Party of both The House of Councillors and The House of Representatives garnering majority support within the Diet. The drafted bill brings a handful of reforms to the table, citing increased tax incentives to families with children. This includes increased incentives, tax breaks, and state healthcare for families with more children. Additionally the Diet proposed the creation of numerous State Controlled childcare centers within more populated regions throughout Japan, providing for the care, education, and well being for children in the stead of parents who may not be able to give up their jobs in lieu of staying at home. Budget analysts estimate a social projects spending increase of a minimum 2% in order to support these reforms. The bill is set to be signed into law by the end of the year.
